name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: A light electric motorcycle: its motor produces 5 gross brake horsepower (3,750 W) or less, the electric counterpart of a motorcycle under 150 cc.

restrictions.rule: A motorcycle: a seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground (California Vehicle Code §405)

Its motor produces 5 gross brake horsepower (3,750 W) or less; one under 3,000 W is a motor-driven cycle rather than a moped when it can go faster than 30 mph (California Vehicle Code §405, as amended by SB 1167 (2026))
The line is drawn only by an engine under 150 cc, which an electric motor doesn't have (California Vehicle Code §405)
Built for highway use: meets federal motor vehicle safety standards, with a 17-digit VIN and a safety certification label (California Vehicle Code §405, as amended by SB 1167 (2026))
Riders need a driver's license with an M1 motorcycle endorsement
Riders must wear a motorcycle helmet
Registered and plated with the DMV, and must carry liability insurance
Barred from any freeway or expressway where Caltrans or the local authority posts a prohibition
Not allowed on bike paths or trails
A vehicle, not property: it can be towed or impounded
